scenes.say: Ever wonder why OnPush makes Angular apps faster? How does it actually detect changes?

rows.b: Checks only on input ref change
Also triggers on events or async

scenes.say: Angular's default strategy checks every component. OnPush checks only when input references change, or when events, observables, or async pipes fire. Signals, new in Angular version seventeen, trigger updates precisely when their value changes.
If you mutate an object directly, OnPush won't notice. But if you replace the reference, Angular triggers an update.
Here's how you set OnPush in a component. Signals, like mySignal here, update the view as soon as their value changes.

scenes.question: What triggers OnPush updates?
scenes.right: Input ref changes, events, observables, async pipes
scenes.say: Don't forget: OnPush updates on input reference changes, but also on events, observables, and async pipes. Missing this can trip you up in interviews.
